title: Connectors (MCP)
summary: An MCP server puts a menu of tools in front of a service. Claude picks a tool and fills in its form; the server makes the real call.
note: Names, companies and files here are **made-up examples**.

props.text: Is Acme up for renewal this quarter?
I can't see your CRM from here. Could you paste Acme's record?

props.title: You are the go-between
props.md: Copy from the CRM, paste into the chat, copy the answer back. Claude knows only what you pasted.

props.title: crm
props.body: A small program that offers Claude a **menu of tools** for one service, and makes the real calls. Unlike a human interpreter, it does only what's on its menu.

props.text: API key: kept in the server's settings

tools.name: find_customer
tools.description: Look up one customer by name: status, owner and renewal date.

tools.name: log_call
tools.description: Add a note about a call to a customer's record.

props.title: Your CRM
props.body: Your customer records, online, with an **API** at `api.example.com`: it answers only fixed-format requests that carry a key.

props.title: On your Mac
props.body: Claude Code starts the server as a program on your computer and talks to it through its text in and text out (**stdio**). Good for your own files and scripts.

props.title: On the service's computers
props.body: Claude Code reaches it over the internet (**HTTP**), often after you sign in once. The recommended way to connect to an online service.

props.title: Connect only servers you trust
props.md: A server typically acts with whatever access its key or sign-in allows, and text it fetches (a web page, an email) can carry hidden instructions: **prompt injection**. Your permission settings still decide what needs your OK.

props.title: See your connectors
props.expect: Start Claude Code, type `/mcp` and press Return. It lists the servers you've connected, whether each one is connected, and how many tools each offers.

steps.title: Copy and paste
steps.text: Claude Code can't see your CRM, the online system that holds your customer records. Without a connector, you are the go-between, and Claude knows only what you pasted.

steps.title: A server at the counter
steps.text: An **MCP server** stands at the service's counter like an interpreter holding a printed menu. **MCP** is the open standard for this. Claude Code is the *host*. For each server it makes an MCP *client*: not a customer, but the part of Claude Code that keeps one connection to that server.

claude.text: I can reach your CRM through the **crm** server now.

steps.title: The menu
steps.text: Each tool has a **name**, a **description** in plain words and an **input form**: the boxes to fill in, with * on the required ones. (Servers can also offer files to read and ready-made prompts; this page sticks to tools.)

steps.title: Claude picks and fills in
steps.text: Claude matches your question to the descriptions, picks `find_customer` and fills in the form: very likely the right choice, not guaranteed, so clear descriptions matter. Claude Code names the call after the server, then the tool.

claude.text: I'll look Acme up in the CRM.

tools.name: find_customer
tools.description: Look up one customer by name: status, owner and renewal date.

tools.name: log_call
tools.description: Add a note about a call to a customer's record.

steps.title: The server makes the call
steps.text: The server turns the form into a real **API** request, adds the key and hands the reply back to Claude. The key stays in the server's settings: Claude's form has no box for it. Servers are usually built so the same form makes the same request every time: that's design, not an MCP rule.

claude.text: Yes: Acme renews on **15 November**, and the account is active.

steps.title: Local or remote
steps.text: A **local** server is a program Claude Code starts on your Mac and talks to through text in and out (*stdio*). A **remote** server runs on the service's own computers and is reached over the internet (*HTTP*).

steps.title: Menus take desk space
steps.text: Every tool definition takes room on Claude's desk, its **context window**. **Tool search**, on by default, loads only the tool names at the start and fetches a tool's full definition when Claude needs it.

steps.title: Trust what you connect
steps.text: The whole picture: you ask, Claude picks a tool and fills in the form, the server makes the call. Connect only servers you trust; Claude Code's permissions still apply (see *Permissions and undo*).
